title: Empirical directed task-transfer matrix
hypothesis: Useful KS/SI/ER transfer is directional or pair-selective, so one symmetric dense Omega cannot represent it.
outcome: weakened: raw ER-directed asymmetry was dominated by task-count-dependent optimizer exposure; KS residual unresolved and SI residual negative after step matching

title: Exposure-controlled gradient compatibility baseline

evaluation.er_protocol: ordinary split for diagnostic evidence only; no ER performance claim

hypothesis: At least one task pair has persistent shared-parameter gradient conflict, norm dominance, or phase-dependent compatibility that classical MTRL's learned Omega does not represent or mitigate.
outcome: confirmed norm-dominance branch: baseline ER shared-gradient norm ratios averaged 7.243 middle and 8.962 late, exceeding 3 in both phases for 5/5 seeds; MTRL ratios were 7.129 and 9.004 and did not consistently improve. Persistent pairwise conflict was rejected. Omega magnitude saturated in 5/5 seeds, with one ER-edge sign flip.
decision: CONFIRMED diagnostic; targeted literature search is next, with no mechanism promoted
